shortDefinition: When an AI confidently generates incorrect or fabricated information.
fullDefinition: Hallucination occurs when an AI model generates text that sounds plausible but is factually wrong or completely invented. This happens because LLMs predict the next most probable token — they have no built-in fact-checking mechanism. Hallucinations can be subtle (slightly wrong dates) or dramatic (entirely fabricated citations).
examples: Confidently citing a paper that doesn't exist
Inventing biographical details about a real person
Getting a historical date slightly wrong with no indication of uncertainty
